Can I hire a nanny for a holiday in Cape Town?

Yes. We place holiday nannies with visiting families across Cape Town and the Western Cape, from a few hours to full-day and live-in cover. Tell us your dates, where you are staying and the ages of your children, and we match you with a vetted nanny before you arrive.
How much does a nanny cost per day in South Africa?

For visiting families, daily care starts at R2,200 for a 10-hour day, and hourly cover starts at R300 an hour with a four-hour minimum. Live-in cover starts at R2,250 a day for longer stays. Travel and overnight fees are quoted separately.
Is it safe to travel to Cape Town with a toddler?

Cape Town is well set up for young children, with good private healthcare, family-friendly beaches and short travel times between the main areas. Like any city it has areas to avoid, so most families base themselves on the Atlantic Seaboard, in the Southern Suburbs or the Winelands. A trusted local nanny adds an extra set of hands and can give you the local insight, suggest hidden gems and help avoid common pitfalls.
Do Cape Town villas provide childcare?

Some luxury villas arrange childcare on request, but many do not, and quality varies. Rather than rely on whoever is free on the day, most families book a vetted nanny in advance and have her come to the villa. We place nannies at villas across the Atlantic Seaboard, Constantia and the Winelands.
Can I take a nanny with us on safari from Cape Town?

Yes. Our nannies travel with families on safari and other trips within South Africa. She minds the children during game drives, early mornings and downtime, so you can relax. Travel, accommodation and overnight fees are agreed upfront. Many Western and Eastern Cape reserves are malaria-free, which suits young children.
How do I find childcare for a destination wedding in Franschhoek?

We provide event nannies for weddings in Franschhoek and across the Winelands. One or more nannies mind the children during the ceremony and reception, run age-appropriate activities, and handle meals and bedtime, so parents and guests can enjoy the day. Book early, as Winelands wedding season fills up fast.
What's the difference between a nanny and an au pair in South Africa?

In South Africa the two terms overlap, and "au pair" is the more common search word. Broadly, a nanny focuses on hands-on care, routines and younger children, while an au pair often drives, helps with homework and does school runs for older kids. We place both, matched to what your household needs.
Do I need a visa or paperwork for a nanny travelling with us in South Africa?

No visa is needed. Our nannies are based in South Africa, so they travel with you inside the country without any immigration paperwork. We put a written agreement in place covering dates, hours, travel and fees before the trip. You confirm the arrangements and the travel details.
How far in advance should I book a holiday nanny in Cape Town?

Book as early as you can. Visiting families usually book four to six months ahead, and the December to January peak and the Easter wave go first. Later requests are still worth making, as we sometimes have availability, but early booking gives you the best choice of nanny.
Can I meet the nanny before we travel?

Yes, always. Under our Meet-First Commitment you speak with the nanny by video call before you travel, or meet in person before a placement starts. There is no obligation to go ahead. We would rather you say no early than feel unsure when she arrives on the first day.
What does a nanny in Cape Town earn per month?

Nanny pay in Cape Town varies with hours, experience, whether the role is live-in, and the ages of the children. For visiting families our daily care starts at R2,200 for a 10-hour day, and live-in cover starts at R2,250 a day on monthly stays. Local family pricing is bespoke and quoted per household.
Are nannies in South Africa First Aid trained?

Every Omega nanny holds a current first aid certificate before we place them. Our current provider is Safe Kids and covers Infant and Child CPR, Choking and Basic First Aid course and renewed every two years. Standards across the wider market vary, so always ask an agency to show proof rather than take a claim on trust.
What is a police clearance certificate and why does it matter?

A SAPS Police Clearance Certificate is an official document from the South African Police Service confirming a person has no relevant criminal record. For childcare it is a fundamental safety check. We require a clear certificate on file before any nanny is placed with a family, so you are not relying on our word.
Can I hire a nanny who speaks German / French / Dutch in Cape Town?

English is standard across our roster, and we work with visiting families from the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and beyond. A bilingual nanny or travel companion, fluent in a requested second language such as French or German, is available as an add-on tier. Tell us the language and dates.
Do nannies in Cape Town drive?

Many do, and a driver's licence is useful for school runs, outings and getting between the beaches, Winelands and town. Some families need a driving nanny, others do not. Tell us if it matters for your placement and we will match a nanny who holds a valid licence.
What's the difference between a night nanny and a night nurse?
Both cover the night, in different ways. A night nanny handles feeds, settling, nappy changes and bedtime routines so you sleep, while a night nurse has clinical training for medical needs.
How do I find a nanny experienced with additional needs in Cape Town?

Ask specifically, and ask what that experience means in practice. Our Special Needs and Teaching Nanny service covers additional learning, developmental and care needs. We have nannies with relevant experience, including a qualified preschool teacher who has worked with additional needs. Tell us your child's needs and we match accordingly.
Is a live-in nanny normal in South Africa?

Yes. Live-in childcare is common and well understood in South Africa, for both local and relocating families. A live-in nanny becomes part of the household routine, covering school runs, homework, meals and bedtime. Accommodation, hours and time off are agreed in writing before the placement starts.
What should I pay a live-in nanny in Cape Town?

Live-in pay depends on hours, days off, experience and the ages of the children. For visiting families our 24/7 live-in cover starts at R2,250 a day on monthly stays, R2,700 a day weekly, and R3,500 a day for short bookings. Local live-in pricing is bespoke and quoted per household.
How do I find childcare when relocating to Cape Town?

Sort it before you arrive. Relocating and semigration families often need a nanny in place from day one, especially with the January back-to-school surge. Tell us your suburb, your move date and your children's ages, and we will line up vetted options so childcare is settled when you land.
